content: The College of Family Physicians of Canada (CFPC) serves as the authoritative voice for family medicine within Canada. Representing over 18,000 members nationwide, it is the professional organization responsible for setting the standards for the training, certification, and ongoing education of family physicians. Additionally, the CFPC advocates on behalf of family medicine, family physicians, and their patients. The CFPC accredits postgraduate family medicine training programs at all 17 medical schools across Canada. Notably, Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, as a member of the Canadian Royal Family, holds the title of Honorary Member of the College. The official journal of the CFPC is the Canadian Family Physician. This peer-reviewed journal, which focuses on research and clinical practice, is published on a monthly basis. It is the only peer-reviewed family medicine journal in Canada that is indexed in major databases such as PubMed Central, MEDLINE, EMBASE/Excerpta Medica, CINAHL, and Current Contents/Clinical Practice. All research and clinical review articles undergo rigorous evaluation by at least two external reviewers, in addition to the editorial staff, to ensure the accuracy and relevance of the content. The journal has a circulation of 35,000 and operates as an open-access publication, making its content freely available. It is important to note that the CFPC should not be confused with regulatory and by-law-setting organizations, such as the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario.
